correctness.rationale: For continuous nonnegative φ≥φ(0), the cited polar-reduction lemma identifies ordinary norm attainment with the decomposable 2-by-2 field M_t over B=|A*|. In its spectral integral a norming vector must have support on Ω={t:||M_t||=L}; if E_B(Ω)=0, positive deficiency L²−||M_t||² on its whole support forbids equality. If projection nonzero, a measurable top eigenspace section of M_t*M_t (matrix dimension two) on a nonzero E_B(Ω) subspace gives equality. This proves iff including non-atomic maximizer sets. Independently checked the example: for t≤r, sqrt(t²+φ(t)²)=t/r, for r≤t≤1 equals one; L²[0,1] multiplication A has no eigenvalue 1 but E_A([r,1])≠0. No finite experiment substitutes for the spectral theorem.
